newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended firmer after they came up for air on Thursday amid very light volume. There was little news on the domestic and foreign fronts to offer direction.
"Today we saw nothing, and I don't expect anything tomorrow. There may be something more in the morning, when London's Liffe will be open," a dealer in Madrid said.
"Prices rose only because there was no volume," he added.
Long-term March futures closed at 111.82, 27 basis points higher, after moving between 111.56 and 111.82. Technical analysts put the next resistance at 111.89.
The 10-year spread over German Bunds declined to 118 basis points from 120 basis points this morning, but German bond market was closed for Christmas both in Frankfurt and at London's Liffe.
Spain's Congress of Deputies, the lower chamber, is expected to give final approval for the 1997 budget law on Friday.
Approval should not be a problem and is considered largely discounted in bond prices already, dealers said.
